newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS MAINLY HIGHER ON FIRMER BRENT.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS MAINLY HIGHER ON FIRMER BRENT.

text.p: European oil swaps were on Tuesday mainly seen regaining some of the ground lost earlier in the week, mainly on the back of crude futures gains.
Heavy fuel swaps edged up 50 cents a tonne, tracking firmer barge levels and firmer Brent but dealers said activity remains slow.
High sulphur barges talked $94.00 for August, $94.75 for September and $95.00 for November while Mediterranean cargo swaps traded at $83.25 for August.
Low sulphur was better bid with talk around $96.50 for August, $98.25 for September and $99.25 for October.
The fourth and first quarters were $5.50 above correspodning barge levels of $97 and $99.
Brent CFDs were little changed. Weekly levels were pegged at around 33 cents under October for the next three weeks but monthly levels remain in contango.
September and October talk 32 cents under the front line IPE but the fourth quarter talks 25 cents under while the first quarter next year talks 12 cents under.

Gasoil cracks against crude were seen unchanged at around $4.45 for fourth quarter, $4.40-$4.50 for first quarter 1998, around $4.00 for the second quarter and $4.40-$4.50 for the third as dealers concentrated on August expiry.
EN590, 0.2 diesel and jet swap differentials were all seen marginally lower for the second day running after declines in end-Monday published physical quotes.
A broker said a 0.2 trade had been struck late Monday at $2.75 for this fourth quarter, confirming a $0.25 overnight drop.
Jet was Tuesday also talked $0.25 down at around $19.50 for September and at $22.00-$22.50 for October, although the outer months and quarters remained unchanged.
Gasoline swaps were quoted $1-$2 up on higher crude futures and a deal-dry barge market at $209-$210 for August, $193-$194.50 for September and $186-$188 for October.

One broker said he had been bidding at $2.95 on the fourth quarter crack, and quoted first and second quarter crack values at $3.31-$3.55 and $4.65-$4.8 respectively, indicating lower bid but unchanged offer levels.
Naphtha front month swaps were also seen responding to crude with gains of $1 to $191-$192 for August and $186.50-$187 for September, brokers said.
